title: Cabin Fever - Late Autumn
author: Julian Rivers
text:
The mountain air had turned bitter by four in the afternoon. Julian pulled his wool collar tighter as the wind whipped across the porch of the remote Tahoe cabin.

Inside, the hearth was already blazing. Marcus looked up from the wooden kitchen counter, where two mugs of black coffee were steaming against the chill. His sleeves were rolled past his forearms, dark curls slightly damp from the afternoon hike.

"You took your time out there," Marcus said quietly, his voice low and raspy in the quiet room. "I was starting to think you got lost in the pines."

Julian closed the heavy timber door behind him, bolting it against the storm. He stepped closer, shaking off the cold. "Not lost. Just thinking."

Marcus set his mug down with a soft click against the granite. His gaze lingered on Julian's lips, then lifted to meet his eyes. The tension that had simmered between them for three days in isolation suddenly felt electric. "Stop thinking so much."

When Marcus stepped forward, his chest brushed Julian's jacket. The warmth radiating from him was intoxicating, smelling of cedarwood, bitter coffee, and rain. Marcus reached up, his leather-gloved thumb gently brushing Julian's jawline before pulling off the glove and pressing warm skin against cold cheek.

Julian let out a shaky exhale. "Marcus..."

"Tell me to stop now, or don't say another word," Marcus whispered against his ear. His breath was hot, sending shivers racing down Julian's spine.

Julian didn't answer with words. He reached out, his hands gripping the front of Marcus's heavy flannel shirt, pulling him in until their mouths crashed together with fierce, desperate hunger.

*~*~*~*~*~*~*~*~*~*~*~*~*~*~*~*~*~*~*~*~*~*~*~*~*

The fluorescent lights of the trauma wing hummed at 2:00 AM. Dr. Bennett adjusted his stethoscope, rubbing his eyes after ten continuous hours on triage. The hospital was finally quiet, except for the distant beep of monitors.

"You look like hell, Doc," a deep voice murmured from behind the nurses' station desk.

Bennett turned to see Officer Miller leaning against the partition, his dark uniform immaculate, muscular shoulders broad against the dim light. Miller had brought in a suspect three hours ago and somehow hadn’t left yet.

"Flattery won’t get you free coffee, Officer," Bennett replied, trying to suppress the smile tugging at the corner of his lips.

Miller pushed off the wall and stepped into the small on-call break room, motioning for Bennett to follow. "Who said anything about coffee?"

*~*~*~*~*~*~*~*~*~*~*~*~*~*~*~*~*~*~*~*~*~*~*~*~*

title: The Penthouse Elevator
author: D. Vance
text:
The elevator jerked violently, shuddered once, and ground to an abrupt halt between the 42nd and 43rd floors. The emergency amber lights flickered on.

Christian adjusted his bespoke silk tie, his breathing steady despite the silence. Beside him stood Liam, his rival senior partner at Sterling & Croft.

"Three hours before the board vote," Liam muttered, loosening his collar with irritation. "Of all the days for hydraulic failure."

Christian turned to face him, eyes dark and calculating. "You're nervous, Liam."

"I'm trapped in a shoebox with the man trying to take my firm," Liam shot back, stepping into Christian's personal space. "What do you expect?"

Christian took a single deliberate step forward, eliminating the remaining inches between them. "I expect you to stop pretending you care about the board vote right now."

Liam's pulse visibly hammered in his throat. "Christian..."

"You've been glaring at me across conference tables for six months," Christian said in a dangerously low voice, pinning Liam against the mirrored steel wall. "Tell me I'm wrong."
